audit.whatIsWrong: Three stages contradict the page's own whys[]. whys[2] says 'that swing is yours to take' but Level 3 is scored Singed; whys[4] calls Feast 'your one hard spike' but Level 6 is scored Skill; whys[6] ends 'call it even' but 2+ items is scored Singed.
audit.why: The packet chart matches all seven whys. Level 3 is the one stage where Cho'Gath has a real punish — a greedy melee last-hit into Rupture plus Feral Scream, with the knockup interrupting Fling. Level 6 is Cho'Gath's outright: Feast's true damage is the only thing in the lane that threatens a health-stacking Singed. At two items neither can finish the other, so it is even.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) Fling is labelled W twice ('Fling (W) you into his minions', 'his W Fling and move speed') — Fling is E and Mega Adhesive is W. (b) 'true damage that ignores Singed's stacked HP and his Mega Adhesive/armor' — true damage does not ignore health, and Mega Adhesive is a ground-slow zone, not a defensive stat. (c) FABRICATED, three occurrences: 'Vorpal Spikes (E) percent-max-HP magic damage'. Riot's text for Vorpal Spikes is 'attacks release deadly spikes, dealing damage and slowing all enemy units in front of him' — no max-health component anywhere, and the kit file's only flags on E are slow. The percentHealth flag in Cho'Gath's kit sits on Feast (R), not E. (d) MISSING: Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, which directly shuts off Carnivore — the passive Cho'Gath's whole lane survival runs on. (e) MISSING: Fling roots only when it lands the target inside Mega Adhesive, so the real combo is goo first, flip second.
audit.why: Riot text — Singed W Mega Adhesive: 17/16/15/14/13s, 1000 range, 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it'. Singed E Fling: 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, 125 range, 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' Singed R Insanity Potion: 100s flat, 'making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds'. Singed Q Poison Trail: NO cooldown at all. Cho'Gath P Carnivore: 'Whenever Cho'Gath kills a unit, he recovers Health and Mana.' Note the grounding on Mega Adhesive is dead weight in this matchup specifically — Cho'Gath has no dash for it to deny, which is why I did not sell it.
audit.corrected: Slot letters fixed in wants.foe[1] and whys[0]; the true-damage claim restated as ignoring armour and MR in spikes[1].text; the invented Vorpal Spikes max-health scaling removed from spikes[3].text and whys[6]; the Grievous Wounds / Carnivore interaction added to dontsFull[2], report[5].t, phases[4].why and spikes[3].text; the goo-then-flip root order added to dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns.
